content.definition: Assets lacking physical substance but providing future economic benefits
content.recognition: Recognize as asset if: (1) Meets definition of asset, (2) Specifically identifiable, (3) Future benefits probable, (4) Cost measurable

finite_lived_intangibles.accounting: AMORTIZE over useful life (not to exceed legal/contractual life)
finite_lived_intangibles.amortization_method: Straight-line unless another method more appropriate
finite_lived_intangibles.residual_value: Usually zero unless third party committed to purchase or active market exists
finite_lived_intangibles.impairment: Test when indicators present (similar to long-lived assets - ASC 360)

indefinite_lived_intangibles.definition: Intangibles with no foreseeable limit on useful life
indefinite_lived_intangibles.accounting: DO NOT amortize. Test for impairment ANNUALLY.
indefinite_lived_intangibles.impairment_test: One-step: Compare FV to carrying amount. If FV < CA, recognize impairment loss.
indefinite_lived_intangibles.note: Goodwill has separate impairment test (covered in goodwill file)

internally_developed_vs_purchased.purchased_intangibles: Capitalize at cost (purchase price + directly attributable costs)

internally_developed.general_rule: EXPENSE as incurred (R&D costs, startup costs, advertising)
internally_developed.exception_software: Capitalize costs after technological feasibility established (ASC 985)
internally_developed.exception_website: Capitalize certain website development costs in development stage

patents.accounting: Amortize over SHORTER of legal life or useful life
patents.internally_developed: Expense R&D costs. Capitalize only legal/registration fees.
patents.purchased: Capitalize purchase price, amortize over useful life

copyrights.accounting: Amortize over expected period of benefit (usually much shorter than legal life)

trademarks.accounting: If intend to renew indefinitely: Indefinite-lived (no amortization). If not: Finite-lived (amortize).
trademarks.internally_developed: Expense advertising/promotion costs. Capitalize only legal/registration fees.

franchises.indefinite_term: No amortization, test for impairment annually

customer_lists.purchased: Capitalize and amortize over expected benefit period

research_and_development.general_rule: Expense ALL R&D costs as incurred
research_and_development.definition: Research = planned investigation to discover new knowledge. Development = translation of research into design for new product/process.
exceptions: Materials/equipment with ALTERNATIVE future use: Capitalize as asset, depreciate
R&D performed for others under contract: Capitalize as inventory or contract asset
research_and_development.software_development_exception: Expense until technological feasibility. Capitalize thereafter (ASC 985).

startup_costs.definition: One-time costs to begin operations (organizing corporation, training, pre-opening costs)
startup_costs.accounting: EXPENSE as incurred (not capitalized as intangible asset)

amortization_calculation.formula: Cost / Useful life (straight-line) or based on units of production
amortization_calculation.example: Patent purchased for $100K, useful life 10 years. Amortization: $100K / 10 = $10K per year. DR Amortization Expense $10K, CR Patent (or Accumulated Amortization) $10K.

impairment_finite_lived.test: Two-step like long-lived assets (ASC 360): (1) Recoverability test using undiscounted cash flows, (2) If not recoverable, impairment = CA - FV

impairment_indefinite_lived.test: One-step: FV vs. CA. If FV < CA, impairment = CA - FV
impairment_indefinite_lived.qualitative_assessment: May perform qualitative assessment first. If more-likely-than-not FV > CA, skip quantitative test.

comparison_to_goodwill.intangibles: Separately identifiable, may be finite or indefinite-lived
comparison_to_goodwill.goodwill: Not separately identifiable, always indefinite-lived, different impairment test (reporting unit level)

calculation_example.facts: Company acquires: Patent $50K (useful life 10 years), Trademark $30K (indefinite), Customer list $20K (5-year life).
calculation_example.year_1_entries: DR Amortization Expense $9K, CR Accumulated Amortization - Patent $5K, CR Accumulated Amortization - Customer List $4K
calculation_example.impairment_test: Trademark tested annually for impairment. Patent and customer list tested if indicators present.

cpa_exam_tips: Finite-lived: AMORTIZE. Indefinite-lived: NO amortization, annual impairment test.
Internally developed intangibles (except software/website): EXPENSE as incurred
R&D costs: EXPENSE as incurred (except materials/equipment with alternative use)
Patents: Capitalize purchase price or legal fees. Amortize over shorter of legal or useful life.
Trademarks: If renewable indefinitely and intend to renew = indefinite (no amortization)
Startup costs: Expense as incurred (not capitalized)
Impairment: Finite-lived = two-step (like PPE). Indefinite-lived = one-step (FV vs CA).

classification_decision: 3. Indefinite → No amortization, annual impairment test
common_mistakes: Using legal life instead of useful life for amortization (use shorter)
Confusing intangible impairment test with goodwill impairment test

key_points: Finite-lived intangibles: Amortize over useful life, test for impairment when indicators present
Indefinite-lived intangibles: No amortization, test annually for impairment
Internally developed intangibles: Generally expense as incurred (except software, website)
Patents: Amortize over shorter of legal or useful life
Trademarks: Indefinite if renewable and intend to renew
Impairment: Finite = two-step. Indefinite = one-step (FV vs CA).
